title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
description:
You have `k` lists of sorted integers in **non-decreasing order**. Find the **smallest** closed range `[a, b]` that includes at least one number from each of the `k` lists.

We define the range `[a, b]` to be smaller than range `[c, d]` if `b - a < d - c`, or if `b - a == d - c` and `a < c`.

Return the smallest range as a two-element integer array `[a, b]`.
constraints: nums[i] is sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Maintain one active element from each of the k lists. The tightest range covering those k chosen elements is `[min_val, max_val]`.
To potentially shrink `[min_val, max_val]`, you must advance the pointer of whichever list currently holds `min_val` (advancing any other list can only increase `max_val`).
Use a min-heap of size k storing `(value, listIndex, elemIndex)` while tracking the running `curMax`. Stop as soon as the list supplying the minimum runs out of elements.

examples.explanation: Range [20, 24] contains 24 from list 1, 20 from list 2, and 22 from list 3, with length 4.
Every list contains 1, so the zero-width range [1, 1] covers all three lists.
Ranges [1, 3], [3, 5], and [5, 7] all cover both lists with length 2, and [1, 3] wins the tie-breaker because 1 < 3 < 5.
